name: NaNoWriMo
seoDesc: NaNoWriMo: work out goal from the end date and the target words per day. A free other calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Give the NaNoWriMo calculator the end date, the target words per day, the days left and the words left and it returns goal. It is built for whatever you happen to be working on. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the NaNoWriMo calculator work?
sections.html:
The NaNoWriMo calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports goal in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you give the end date; then you type in the target words per day, the days left, the words left and the total writing time.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A calendar date. Use the picker; the answer is recalculated the moment the date changes, and the count is done date-to-date rather than by subtracting timestamps.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in percent. The unit chip switches it to any of the 6 supported units.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.
  • A number, expressed in words.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in hours / minutes. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the NaNoWriMo calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Goal=words left + current word count
Your average per day=current word count ÷ (-start date + today is... + 1)
Today is=-days left + end date + 1
Words per day to reach goal=words left ÷ days left
Goal=current word count ÷ you've done...
At this rate, you'll finish on...=today is... + words left ÷ your average per day

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Open the page and it is already filled in. With the values it starts from — Goal = 50000 and Words per minute = 15 — it reports Total writing time = 0.9259 hrs.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Total writing time = 0.9259 hrs should be roughly the size you expected from Goal = 50000 and Words per minute = 15.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • %, opening in percent
  • Time, opening in hours / minutes
  • Time, opening in hours / minutes
  • Time, opening in hours / minutes

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The NaNoWriMo calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the end date, the target words per day and the days left — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Dates are compared date to date in your own time zone, so a daylight-saving change will not shift the count by a day.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the NaNoWriMo calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns goal, derived from the end date, the target words per day and the days left. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the NaNoWriMo calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the end date, the target words per day, the days left and the words left, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter you've done... in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. You've done opens in percent and the chip beside it offers 6 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Total writing time = 0.9259 hrs. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the NaNoWriMo calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
